newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: New Zealand share prices end lower after jobs data.
newsitem.headline: New Zealand share prices end lower after jobs data.

text.p: * NZ share prices end lower after strong jobs number
* Brokers see little chance of easing, short term
* Volume picks up, but mostly in off-market trades
Price movements at close
LAST CHG * NZSE40 cap index -14.88 at 2,543.91

New Zealand share prices ended on their lows for the day after stronger-than-expected employment data removed short-term hopes of a further easing of monetary conditions by the Reserve Bank.
The NZSE-40 Capital Index ended 14.88 points down at 2,543.91 on turnover worth NZ$61 million - about half of that transacted offmarket or before the opening.
Jobs data for the June quarter showed employment growth had risen a seasonally adjusted 0.2 percent while most analysts had expected a small decline.
The Reserve Bank later said that the data did nothing to alter their assessment of that state of the economy since its June monetary policy statement.
"There really was not enough information there for the Reserve Bank to say 'yes, we'll have a bit of an easing'," Nigel Scott at BZW said.
"So the market had a bit of sell-off around midday, basically because of a lack of direction out of those figures," he said.
Fletcher Forests, down one cent at to $1.98, Brierley Investments, and Fletcher Energy, down seven cents at NZ$1.98, were among those to be actively traded.
Fernz Corp, which reported its result last week, was another actively traded stock, losing five to NZ$5.20.
